title: Hosting pathway blueprint sketch
content:
Executive summary:

This is a lightweight, workshop-driven blueprint for deciding between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment paths during customer PoCs. The goal is to give SEs a rapid decision flow and a practical migration/cutover checklist that balances time-to-value, predictable latency, data control, and operational burden.

Context and assumptions (quick):
- Redwood product surfaces available: Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), Console observability, Optimize suggestions, routing/fallback policies.
- Typical PoC horizons: 4–12 weeks.
- Common constraints we see: strict data sovereignty, predictable P95 SLAs, bursty traffic patterns, and enterprise procurement timelines.
- Target metrics for decisioning: p50/p95 generation latency, cost per 1M tokens, time-to-production (TTProd), and ops maintenance FTE/month.

Decision flow (one-page mental model):
1) Data sensitivity and compliance gates:
   - If regulated data cannot leave customer network and cannot be transferred to cloud-managed control plane -> Private (VPC or on-prem).
   - If IP/data is sensitive but can be supported with strict contracts and region restrictions -> Dedicated (reserved capacity in customer-region) or Hosted with strict region routing + contractual terms.
2) Latency & UX requirements:
   - <100ms p95 and small prompt sizes -> Evaluate Dedicated with colocated GPUs (or Private on-prem) + aggressive KV cache.
   - 100–600ms acceptable -> Hosted can often satisfy with model selection and edge routing.
3) Throughput and scaling dynamics:
   - Very bursty (spiky) workloads with unpredictable spikes -> Hosted for elasticity and pay-for-use; add Dedicated burst buckets if predictability needed.
   - Predictable high sustained throughput -> Dedicated (reserve capacity) to reduce unit costs.
4) Time-to-deploy/Procurement:
   - Need results in 2–4 weeks -> Hosted (fastest).
   - 4–12 weeks and procurement possible -> Dedicated.
   - >12 weeks + heavy legal procurement -> Private.

Comparison matrix (short):
Columns: Hosted | Dedicated | Private
- Time-to-deploy: very fast | moderate | slow
- Cost profile: variable, pay-as-you-go | predictable reserved | high fixed + predictable
- Latency predictability: medium | high | highest (if on-prem colocated)
- Data isolation: shared | tenant-isolated | customer-controlled
- Ops overhead (customer): low | medium | high
- Scaling elasticity: high | moderate (with burst) | low to moderate
- Compliance fit (sovereignty): limited | good (region-level) | best

Three quick vignettes (recommendations):
1) Fintech conversational KYC assistant (must retain PII in-region, <200ms p95)
   - Recommendation: Dedicated in customer region.
   - Rationale: Predictable latency and contractual isolation. Use reserved capacity with 2x headroom, KV prefix cache for account histories, strict routing to customer-region GPU pools.
   - Topology sketch: Customer region Dedicated pool -> VPC peering for audit logs -> Console tracing hooked to customer S3 audit bucket (read-only).
2) High-volume ecommerce search/ranking reranker (2–3M requests/day, bursty traffic around events)
   - Recommendation: Hosted + Dedicated burst lanes (mixed).
   - Rationale: Hosted handles spikes and elasticity; Dedicated reserved capacity for baseline traffic reduces cost. Use smart routing by cost/latency: baseline to Dedicated, overflow to Hosted.
   - Topology sketch: Edge LB -> Routing policy (cost/latency) -> Dedicated pool (baseline) -> fallback Hosted API. Use caching at CDN edge for idempotent queries.
3) Hospital diagnostics assistant (PHI, air-gapped onboarding)
   - Recommendation: Private (on-prem) with Redwood private control plane or fully air-gapped bundle.
   - Rationale: PHI and audit constraints require on-prem. Plan for HSM/KMS integration and offline model bundles.
   - Topology sketch: On-prem inference cluster (dedicated GPUs) + private control plane via customer-managed VPC + on-prem log forwarder to customer's SIEM.

Migration and rollout pathway (hosted -> dedicated -> private):
- Phases: 1) Discovery & quick PoC on Hosted (2–4 weeks) -> 2) Baseline Dedicated sizing & pilot (4–8 weeks) -> 3) Private pilot for regulated customers (8–16+ weeks)
- Key checkpoints: SLA smoke test (p95 under load), cost forecast review, legal/compliance signoff, DR/restore drill.
- Cutover checklist (recommended):
  - Confirm model version compatibility and weights across environments
  - Validate KV-cache warmup strategy (seed from Hosted logs where permitted)
  - Configure routing and fallback policy: Dedicated primary, Hosted fallback with degradation policy
  - Run load test (10x expected baseline) and capture p50/p95/cold-start metrics
  - Confirm telemetry and trace propagation to Redwood Console and customer observability
  - Security: verify KMS/HSM integration, audit trail access controls
  - Final ops runbook and escalation contacts

Risk register (short, prioritized):
- Risk: Data egress constraints stop Hosted trial mid-PoC.
  - Mitigation: Early legal/data questionnaire; if any red flags, route straight to Dedicated/Private trial.
- Risk: Unexpected p95 latency spikes in Dedicated due to noisy neighbor placement.
  - Mitigation: Reserve extra capacity, enable isolation-first node assignment, monitor p95 with automated scale-up rules.
- Risk: Cost overruns during Hosted overflow to pay-as-you-go.
  - Mitigation: Set hard quotas/alerts and fallback to lower-cost model or rate-limits.
- Risk: Private deployment timeline slips due to procurement/hardware lead times.
  - Mitigation: Prepare a temporary Dedicated bridge and an interim contractual plan.

Operational knobs & tuning notes (practical):
- Use model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs (e.g., distilled model for high-volume, full model for sensitive outputs).
- Configure prefix/KV caching for user sessions to reduce token costs and p95.
- Batching: tune continuous batching windows for throughput-heavy reranking jobs; keep them minimal for strict latency routes.
- Autoscale policies: Dedicated should have headroom and a burst pool; set aggressive scale-up for p95 violations.
- Circuit breaker: on persistent degraded outputs, fallback to lower-cost Hosted variant with reduced capabilities rather than total failure.

Workshop notes / open questions (to capture with customer):
- "What are your legal redlines for data residency and logging?" (capture before choosing Hosted) -> Action: legal questionnaire (JIRA-SEQ-9812).
- "Expected peak concurrency and acceptable throttling behavior?" -> Action: product analytics ask (owner: Marcus) to instrument sample traffic.
- "Do you require HSM integration or can a KMS with RBAC suffice?" -> Action: security scoping (owner: Elena).

Meeting actions (owners & due dates):
- Run hosted smoke PoC with sample traffic and capture p50/p95 (Owner: Devon; due: 2024-11-20)
- Prepare Dedicated sizing estimate (Owner: Ava; due: 2024-11-27)
- Legal/compliance questionnaire to cust (Owner: Solutions AE; due: 2024-11-15)
- Draft migration runbook for hosted->dedicated (Owner: Marcus; due: 2024-12-05)

Notes to SEs (tactical tips):
- Start with Hosted to gather realistic traffic profiles and sample traces; use these traces to size Dedicated pools (we often under- or over-provision without them).
- Use the Console’s route-level cost breakdown early; customers respond well to concrete $/1k token examples.
- If the customer is procurement-heavy, document a bridge: Hosted trial -> Dedicated pilot -> Private contract.

Appendix: quick commandables and references:
- Load test target: sustained baseline * 1.5 and two short spikes at 5x sustained for 5 minutes. Capture p50/p95/99.
- Proxy routing rule example (pseudocode):
   if (region == customerRegion && reservedCapacity.available) route -> DedicatedPool
   else if (burst && reservedCapacity.full) route -> HostedFallback
   else route -> Hosted

Unresolved:
- Customer-specific SLA thresholds and legal egress tolerances (see linked JIRA).

End notes: This doc is intended to be a living sketch for workshop facilitation and handoff to Eng/Product for final architecture. Treat as working notes: please add more topologies and concrete sizing after the first two smoke PoCs.
